sections.name: File setup, PUBLIC, SIGNED_IN_EXTRA
sections.title: Test page list and imports
sections.what: Lists the public pages and the extra signed-in page to test, and brings in the testing tools and helpers.
sections.why: Keeps the page list in one place so adding a page means adding one entry.
sections.watch_out: A new public page must be added to this list or it will not be checked.

sections.name: axe (part 1)
sections.title: Running the accessibility checker
sections.what: Waits for a page to settle, runs the accessibility checker on it, and returns the problems found as short lines naming the rule and the elements.
sections.why: A shared helper keeps every page checked the same way, and waiting first avoids checking a half-loaded page.
sections.watch_out: Only the first three affected elements are listed per rule, so the failure may not show every location.

sections.name: axe (part 2)
sections.title: Keyboard, theme and motion checks
sections.what: Checks that the mobile menu opens from the keyboard, the current page is marked in the desktop navigation, the theme button sets the page theme and survives a reload, and no motion keeps running under reduced motion.
sections.why: These behaviours are easy to break and are specifically required for accessible use.
sections.watch_out: The reduced-motion check waits only a tenth of a second before counting animations, so slow pages may be checked too early.

summary: Browser tests that load each public and signed-in page and check it against accessibility rules, plus keyboard, theme and reduced-motion behaviour.
purpose: Makes sure the app is usable by people who rely on screen readers, keyboards, high-contrast or dark themes, and reduced motion.
why: Accessibility failures are easy to introduce with new pages, so checking every route automatically catches them early.
how: A helper loads a page, waits for the title and for animations to settle, runs the axe accessibility checker against standard WCAG rules, and returns a list of problems. Tests then loop over public pages in light and dark mode, sign in and walk through the crew and match pages, test the mobile menu with keyboard only, check the desktop navigation and theme switch, and confirm animations stop under reduced motion.
inputs: The list of public paths and the signed-in extra paths, plus the browser, the user account made by a helper, and a seeded match.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each page and each scenario. Failures list the rule identifier and the element locations.
risks: Fixed waits such as a short timeout can make the reduced-motion test flaky. The theme test expects a specific light result after clicking, which depends on the current default.
debug: If one page fails, read the rule identifier and element path in the failure. For keyboard or menu failures, check the labels and focus order on that page. For flaky animation tests, check whether the page keeps a running animation.
